verdict.rationale: Buzz describes "YAML-as-code automation" with traces, and offers workflow trigger/approve commands. Its built-in git hosting supports patches, review, CI and protected branches, so automations kept as code could plausibly be versioned and reviewed through repo patches; agent drafts are also owner-reviewed before creation, and persona packs can live in a git repo. However, nothing documents an end-to-end automation versioning or rollback flow, so this is inferred from adjacent capabilities. Missing for 10: explicit docs that workflow definitions are stored and versioned in repos, a documented review flow for automation changes, any rollback or revert mechanism for automations, and hands-on corroboration.
